title: AI Platform Overview
description: Phase 14: end-to-end observability for the AI pipeline - REST, RAG/vector search, LLM/embedding calls, tool calls, and agent/guardrail safety bounds.

panels.title: API latency (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: http.server.requests - every REST endpoint, free from Spring Boot's own web observation filter.

panels.title: Request rate by endpoint
panels.description: Request count, broken down by URI - the free http.server.requests counter.

panels.title: Failures (4xx / 5xx)
panels.description: outcome=CLIENT_ERROR covers guardrail rejections (400/413/429) too - they surface here even without a dedicated counter.

panels.title: LLM (chat) latency p95
panels.description: gen_ai.client.operation.duration, tagged gen_ai_operation_name="chat" - free from Spring AI's chat observation. Confirm the exact tag value against /actuator/prometheus output for your provider.

panels.title: Token usage by type
panels.description: gen_ai.client.token.usage - input/output/total tokens per second, free from Spring AI's chat observation.

panels.title: Vector-search latency p95
panels.description: rag.vector.search - hand-instrumented (Phase 14); measures the pgvector query only, excluding embedding generation.

panels.title: Avg. retrieved documents per search
panels.description: rag.retrieved.documents - hand-instrumented (Phase 14); chunks returned before similarity-threshold filtering.

panels.title: Tool-call latency p95 by tool
panels.description: spring.ai.tool - free from Spring AI's tool-calling observation; reached whether a tool is called in-process (Phase 8) or via MCP (Phase 13).

panels.title: Avg. agent iterations per request
panels.description: agent.iterations - hand-instrumented (Phase 14); how many capability steps the agent workflow executed.

panels.title: Safety bounds triggered, by reason
panels.description: ai.safety.bound.triggered - guardrail rejections and agent safety-bound truncations (Phase 12 + Phase 9), all in one counter family tagged by reason.

panels.title: Spend per hour, by model tier
panels.description: ai.cost.usd - token counts converted to money using app.ai.pricing. Tokens are not comparable across models, so this is the only view that shows whether model tiering is actually working: the fast tier should carry most of the call volume and a small fraction of the spend. A fast-tier line that starts tracking the capable one means something has been quietly repointed at the expensive model.

panels.title: Tokens by tier and type
panels.description: ai.tokens - split into prompt, prompt_cached and completion. prompt_cached is the only evidence that provider-side prompt caching is working; if it stays at zero the stable system-prefix ordering is not being rewarded and the persona is being paid for on every request.

panels.title: Semantic answer cache hit rate
panels.description: ai.answer.cache - a hit skips retrieval AND generation entirely. This is the number that says whether the cache is worth the risk it carries: a semantic cache that is wrong does not return a stale answer, it returns the answer to a different question. Watch it alongside the similarity threshold, and never raise the hit rate by lowering the threshold without evaluation evidence.

panels.title: Candidates found only by the lexical search
panels.description: rag.hybrid.lexical.only - results the full-text half surfaced and the vector half did not. This is whether hybrid retrieval is earning its second query: consistently zero means the lexical search is contributing nothing dense retrieval was not already finding; consistently non-zero means these are results dense-only retrieval was silently missing.

panels.title: Spend per hour, by model
panels.description: The same spend broken down by the model the PROVIDER reported rather than the one requested - an alias resolving to a dated snapshot shows up here and not in the tier view.
